description: DVinyl is a self-hostable collection management platform for collectors. Catalog, organize and track physical media and collectibles with custom item types, rich metadata, multi-collection support, authentication, and powerful import tools.

latest_release.name: v4.0.0 - One File, Your Look, and a Collection That Talks Back
latest_release.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> ⚠️ As always, **export your database before upgrading** (Instance admin page, Backup → Export). Safety first!
>
> 🚚 4.0 moves DVinyl from MongoDB to **SQLite**. **Nothing breaks on update**: an install from 3.x keeps running on its MongoDB until you mount a `data` folder, then moves itself over. Read [Moving to SQLite](./docs/docker.md#-moving-to-sqlite) when it suits you.

Hi everyone! Here is DVinyl **v4.0.0**, the biggest release so far. Your whole collection now lives in **one SQLite file**, with no database container to run. Each collection can pick **its own look**, from the navigation to the colours, the home page and the background. Members can **send each other requests** (a loan, a gift, anything you make up) with **notifications on their phone**. And a very long list of things you asked for is in: purchase prices, record formats and runouts, film casts, Open Library as a full source, consoles beside games, boxsets holding their contents, invite links, automatic backups and much more.

A huge thank you to @Siebe-Uy for the eight trading card game plugins, to @ArtwoXYZ for the local image copies (#136) and the work on custom field overlaps (#151), to @alexeyseo for the whole Russian translation (#220, #221, #222, #230), and to @teaboyteaboy for the back-link fix (#201). Thanks as well to @vic1707 and @Patricol for pushing the move off MongoDB, and to @jcompiet, @Mellow1238, @luqqaa, @mikeycp, @HalbridiousBall, @abr8838-crypto, @KevinCorcor, @lebeanshoe, @reneald, @driph, @theothermillion and everyone in the discussions for the ideas, reports and testing behind this release!

---

## 🗄️ SQLite: Your Collection in One File (#199)

DVinyl no longer needs a MongoDB server. Everything (items, accounts, collections, lists, shelves, settings) is kept in a single `data/dvinyl.sqlite` file.

- **Simpler to run**: one container, no database to keep up, no AVX requirement, and noticeably less memory.
- **Simpler to back up**: one folder holds the whole collection.
- **Built for small hosts**: exports are now streamed item by item, so even a 20,000-item instance exports within a small memory budget.
- **Safe by design**: a container whose `data` folder is not mounted refuses to start (instead of losing everything at the next update), and a second DVinyl pointed at the same folder is refused too.

### Coming from 3.x

You do **not** have to change your configuration on update day:

- As long as no `data` folder is mounted, DVinyl **keeps running on your MongoDB exactly as before**, with a notice on the Instance admin page.
- The first time it starts with a `data` folder mounted, it **copies everything into SQLite by itself**, ids included, so links, lists and share links keep working. MongoDB is only read; a small marker is left on it so the same data is never used or copied twice by mistake.
- Then retire MongoDB whenever you like.

Step-by-step guides for Docker Compose, Unraid, `docker run` and installs from source are in [Moving to SQLite](./docs/docker.md#-moving-to-sqlite), including what each log line means.

> [!NOTE]
> One more reason to move: on recent Linux kernels (6.19 and later), the `mongo:8` images refuse to start, and `mongo:latest` can crash under load. SQLite has no such issue.

---

## 🎨 Make Each Collection Your Own

The whole look of a collection is now gathered in one **studio** (Personalisation), with the live app in a preview frame (any page, desktop, tablet or phone, light or dark) and every choice beside it.

- **Navigation**: a top bar (full width or floating, optionally sticky), a left or right sidebar (expanded or as an icon rail), or a bottom dock.
- **Ready-made styles and layouts**: classic, sidebar, dock, minimal, dense, editorial, previewed and applied in one click.
- **Colours**: a palette worked out from a single colour (neutral, tinted or vivid), adjustable colour by colour with readability warnings, and up to twelve named palettes per

detail.readme:
DVinyl is a self-hosted manager for physical collections: records, books, films, games, LEGO, board games, trading cards, and any kind of item you define yourself.

--- ## Hey there 👋 DVinyl is a little home for your physical collection. It lives on your own server, pulls in cover art and metadata from the big databases (Discogs, Hardcover, Open Library, TMDB, IGDB, ScreenScraper, Rebrickable, BoardGameGeek), can even estimate what your records are worth, and lays it all out on virtual shelves that look like the real ones, in a style you get to shape yourself. Everything lives in one SQLite file: no database server to run. DVinyl is **plugin based**: every media type is a plugin, so you turn on only what you care about, and you can add your own type without touching the core. Want to see it before installing anything? Have a look at the [live demo](https://demo.kyonew.me/), a read-only preview of a finished instance. ## What it can do ### 📦 Your whole shelf, in one place - **Many formats.** Music (vinyls, CDs, cassettes), books (manga, comics, hardcover), movies (Blu-ray, 4K, DVD, VHS, LaserDisc), video games and consoles, LEGO sets, board games and trading card games. - **Your own types.** Collect something else? Create a new type right from the app with the no-code plugin editor, or write a [code plugin](./docs/plugin-development.md) with its own API. - **Collector details.** Record size, speed, pressing plant, mastering and runouts per side from Discogs, film casts and original titles, several formats in one edition, boxsets holding their contents, and what you paid for each copy. - **Multiple views & virtual shelves.** Browse in a grid, a compact table, or as realistic virtual shelves with spine view and customizable furniture. - **Lists & playlists.** Curate custom lists within a collection and assemble tracks into playlists. - **Multiple collections.** Keep separate libraries (yours, the family's, by room) and switch in one click. - **Smart import & barcode scanner.** Add items by ID, scan physical barcodes with your camera, or bulk import existing libraries (Discogs with your own custom fields, Goodreads, any CSV). - **Fast editing.** Edit one field on a whole selection, save and go on to the next item, saved filter views, and table columns per type. - **AI assist.** Bring-your-own-key support for text, photo or barcode-fallback import, and for drafting a new no-code plugin from a one-sentence description. See the [AI Assist guide](./docs/ai.md) to set it up. - **Market value & price history.** Live valuation estimates for your records and cards, with historical charts over time. - **Game completion times.** Playtime estimates powered by IGDB. - **Printable labels.** Generate printable QR codes and barcodes for your physical media. - **Wishlist.** Keep track of items you are hunting for. ### 🎨 Make it yours - **A look per collection.** A studio with a live preview: ready-made styles, a top bar, sidebar or dock, your own colour palettes, fonts, card shapes, logo and background. - **Home page widgets.** Arrange stats, latest additions, wishlist, lists and notes in a grid. - **Collection info page.** Add a rich Markdown presentation page with photos for your collections. - **In your pocket.** Installs on your phone like an app, with the barcode scanner one tap away. - **Multilingual.** English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Russian. ### 👥 Share it, your way - **Users and roles.** Invite people to a collection as admin, editor or viewer, so everyone gets the right level of access, or send them a single-use invite link. - **Requests & notifications.** Members ask each other to borrow an item or offer a gift, under types the admin makes up, with push notifications on their phone. - **See each other's wishes.** Search results show who among your collections' members wishes for a record. - **SSO login (OIDC).** Optional single sign-on with providers like Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia or pocketID, with optional automatic account creation from an identity provider group. - **Public share links.** Generate a read-only link or QR code so anyone can browse a collection (or just part of it, e.g. only Vinyls) without an account. ### 💾 Your data stays yours - **One file.** The whole collection in one SQLite file, easy to back up. - **Backups.** Collection or whole-instance exports (ZIP with images, JSON, CSV), and automatic daily or weekly backups to a folder of your choice. - **Local image copies.** Optionally download the covers that are only links, so they never vanish and travel in your backups. ## Supported media | Type | Formats | Metadata source | API key | | :--- | :------ | :-------------- | :-----: | | Music | Vinyl, CD, cassette | Discogs | ✅ | | Books | Books, manga, comics | Hardcover, Open Library | optional | | Movies | Blu-ray, 4K, DVD, VHS, LaserDisc | TMDB | ✅ | | Video games | Games, consoles | IGDB, ScreenScraper | ✅ | | LEGO | Sets | Rebrickable | ✅ | | Board games | Games, expansions | BoardGameGeek | ✅ | | Trading cards | Pokémon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Lorcana, Star Wars: Unlimited, Digimon, Flesh and Blood | TCGdex, Scryfall, YGOPRODeck and others | none | Each type can be turned on or off per collection. Add only the keys for the types you use: a type whose key is missing stays disabled. See [API keys](./docs/api-keys.md) for where to get each one. ## Build your own type DVinyl is made to grow with you. There are two ways to add a new kind of collection: - **Plugin editor (no code).** Create a manual collection type right from the app, with your own fields, formats, icon and colors. No restart, no coding required. Short on ideas? The AI assist can draft one from a one-sentence description. See the [Plugin editor guide](https://github.com/Kyonew/DVinyl/wiki) on the Wiki. - **Code plugin (with API).** Drop a `plugins//` folder that exports a plugin definition to add a full media type with its own external API, importers and stats. See the [Plugin development guide](./docs/plugin-development.md). Built one you are proud of? Do not hesitate to open a PR, I would genuinely love to see it! 🙌 ## Installation ### Docker Compose (recommended) ```yaml services: dvinyl-app: image: ghcr.io/kyonew/dvinyl:latest container_name: dvinyl_app restart: unless-stopped ports: - "3099:3099" volumes: - ./data:/app/data # the SQLite database - ./public/uploads:/app/public/uploads # uploaded images env_file: - .env ``` Create a `.env` next to it from [.env.example](./.env.example). Two secrets are required: ```bash PASSJWT= # openssl rand -hex 32 SESSION_SECRET= # openssl rand -hex 32, a different one ``` Then start it and open `http://your-server:3099` to create the first account: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` More options (building from source, environment-only setup) are in the [Docker guide](./docs/docker.md). ### Other platforms | Platform | How | | :------- | :-- | | Unraid | Community Applications, or the [XML template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kyonew/DVinyl/main/unraid-template/dvinyl.xml) ([guide](./docs/getting-started.md#-unraid)) | | ZimaOS / CasaOS | Add the source `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NoNoBzH22/TwoBytes-Store/gh-pages` to the App Store, then install DVinyl ([guide](./docs/getting-started.md#-zimaos)) | | Proxmox LXC | A small Debian container, no Docker ([guide](./docs/getting-started.md#-proxmox-lxc)) | | Node.js | Run it directly on any machine ([guide](./docs/getting-started.md)) | ## Configuration All settings live in `.env`; [.env.example](./.env.example) documents every variable. The most common ones: | Variable | Purpose | | :------- | :------ | | `PASSJWT`, `SESSION_SECRET` | Required secrets, two different random values | | `SETUP_TOKEN` | Protects the first-run setup page while the instance is reachable by others | | `PROD` | Set to `true` only when served over HTTPS | | `VINYL_PORT`, `BASE_URL` | Port, and sub-path when served under one | | `PUBLIC_URL`, `PUSH_CONTACT` | Public address, used for links and push notifications | | `BACKUP_DIR` | Forces the folder for scheduled backups | | `DISCOGS_TOKEN`, `TMDB_API_KEY`, `TWITCH_CLIENT_ID`… | Metadata providers ([API keys](./docs/api-keys.md)) | | `OIDC_*` | Single sign-on ([details](./docs/getting-started.md#-environment-variables)) | | `AI_*` | Optional AI import ([AI Assist](./docs/ai.md)) | Behind a reverse proxy? See [the HTTPS section](./docs/getting-started.md#-behind-a-reverse-proxy-https). ## Updating ```bash docker compose pull && docker compose up -d ``` Back up your `data/` folder first, or use the built-in backups. Coming from 3.x (MongoDB), your data is moved to SQLite automatically on first start: read [Moving to SQLite](./docs/docker.md#-moving-to-sqlite) before upgrading. Rolling back is covered in the [Docker guide](./docs/docker.md#rolling-back). ## Documentation | Guide | Content | | :---- | :------ | | [Getting started](./docs/getting-started.md) | Installation options, environment variables, reverse proxy | | [Docker deployment](./docs/docker.md) | Compose setup, updates, persistence, backups | | [API keys](./docs/api-keys.md) | Discogs, Hardcover, TMDB, IGDB, ScreenScraper, Rebrickable, BoardGameGeek | | [AI Assist](./docs/ai.md) | Bring-your-own-key AI import and plugin drafting | | [Plugin development](./docs/plugin-development.md) | Build a media type as a code plugin | | [Public share links](./docs/sharing.md) | Read-only links to a collection | | [Wiki](https://github.com/Kyonew/DVinyl/wiki) | User guides and no-code tutorials | **Tech stack:** Node.js, Express, SQLite, EJS, Tailwind CSS, i18next. ## Contributors DVinyl is better for the people who jumped in. Huge thanks to everyone whose pull requests made it into `main` 💜 (hover an avatar to see their merged PRs)

Want to see your name here? Bug reports, ideas, translations and plugins are all welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Code of Conduct](./.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) first. ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) > [!NOTE] > Parts of the frontend and comments were generated with the help of AI tools. I reviewed and > corrected the output where needed, but this project is not 100% human-made. Feedback is very > welcome, including on the backend, where I may have made mistakes. Thank you for your understanding <3
